summary: Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei, Seoul National, and UCLA (under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Hee-Sung Keel, and Hyon-uk Kim), later serving at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) studied Japanese history at Ryukoku University (~1939–1950), working in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held various faculty and leadership posts at Ryukoku (1950–1989), the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute, and Soai Gakuen.

Jos Gommans (born 1963) is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Radboud University and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink, later serving as a fellow at the Dutch Research Council and associate professor at Leiden (1993).

Josef Horovitz (1874–1931) was a scholar of religious studies and history who completed his doctoral studies under Eduard Sachau (~1895–1898). He held an academic post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick (1859–1944) studied linguistics at Tübingen and Berlin (PhD 1889 under Albrecht Weber). He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, and Heidelberg before serving as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Munich from 1896 to 1925.

Josef Strzygowski (1862–1941) was an art historian who studied at the University of Munich (~1883–1885). He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (~1920–1925).

Josef van Ess (1934–2021) specialized in religious studies. He studied at the University of Bonn from approximately 1953 to 1959 and held a long-term academic post at the University of Tübingen from around 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Campbell (1904–1987) studied religious studies and literature at Columbia, Paris, and Munich. After early teaching at Canterbury School and Columbia, he spent most of his career teaching at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph Dalton Hooker (1817–1911) studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). He worked at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and later served as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew from 1847 to 1885.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg (1928–2018) studied geography and Indology at Brooklyn College, Maryland, the Sorbonne, and Wisconsin under Richard Hartshorne. He taught at Pennsylvania and had a long career at the University of Minnesota (1964–2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter (1844–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at University College School and the University of London, later serving as a religious scholar at Oxford and President of Harris Manchester College (~1876–1915).

Joseph Goldstein (born 1944) studied at Columbia and under numerous Buddhist masters, including Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw. Active in Buddhist studies, he taught at Naropa University (1974) and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center.

Joseph Hackin (1886–1941) was an archaeologist of Central Asia and Buddhism who studied at Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot. He held posts at the Guimet Museum (1907–1941), École du Louvre, and Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan.

Joseph Haroutunian (1904–1968) studied philosophy and religion at the American University of Beirut, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Wellesley College (1932–1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Loizzo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst, Harvard, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, later becoming a Visiting Scholar at Columbia and founding the Nalanda Institute (attested 2007).

Joseph M. Kitagawa (1915–1992) studied religious studies at Rikkyo, CDSP, Seabury, and Chicago under Joachim Wach. He had a long career at the University of Chicago (1951–1987), serving as professor and Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who completed his master's degree at Columbia University (~1948–1950). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University (attested 1991).

Joseph A. Marino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2013–2017) under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, where he also serves as Assistant Professor (attested 2026).

Joseph Needham (1900–1995) studied at Cambridge and Gonville and Caius College. A historian and sinologist, he served as Cambridge Reader in Biochemistry (~1933–1966), Master and Fellow of Caius, and Director of the Needham Research Institute (~1976–1990).
